partner_source.actual_inequality: E|A(U)-s|^{-1/4}|B(V)-t|^{-1/4} <= calB(P), hence P(|A-s|<=r,|B-t|<=r)<=calB(P)sqrt(r), for P_-=P and P_+=-P.

new_results.statement: For independent two-coordinate cap-one product banks X,Y, invertible 2x2 C, arbitrary measurable F and shifts, R=F(X)+(X-a)^T C(Y-b) satisfies sup_s E|R-s|^{-1/2} <= (4/3)2^(7/4)pi^(1/4)|det C|^{-1/4}.
For U=X-X', V=X+X' and matched opposite 2x2 curvatures P,-P with arbitrary affine terms, S=A(U)+B(V) obeys sup_z E|S-z|^{-1/2} <= (4/3)2^(3/4)pi^(1/4)|det P|^{-1/4}.
The whole-copy identity gives int |t|^{-1/2}|phi_S(t)|^2 dt <= (4/3)2^(5/4)pi^(3/4)|det P|^{-1/4}.

For an additional genuinely independent cap-one square d(Z+h)^2, the sum has an essentially bounded density <= (4/3)2^(3/4)pi^(1/4)|d|^{-1/2}|det P|^{-1/4}, hence linear one-copy small-ball scaling. Continuity is not proved.

mathematical_premises: X_i are original independent cap-one coordinates; X' is an independent copy.
U and V are never treated as independent; only their separate marginal product structure is used by the partner theorem.
The new bilinear proof conditions only inside a genuinely independent original product bank.
The transformed vector C^T(X-a) is allowed dependent coordinates; only its joint Jacobian density cap is used.
No moment, compact-support, connected-support, Gaussian or log-concavity assumption is used.
